claims.text: In docs/team/sprint-example.md, 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy' has estimate 2 and final status 'Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau'; the file does not say why it took longer.
The sprint review section says the 'Ngừng gửi thông báo' item was not shown because it was not finished; unfinished work is not counted even with almost all the code written.

The retrospective lists: did well (acceptance criteria before code), needs fixing (work depending on a single person), action (items larger than 3 points must have two people read the code); no line mentions estimates.

An estimate is a guess about size made before the work starts; an item not finishing does not make its estimate wrong; only after the work can the team compare the guess with reality, for example at the retrospective.
Treating estimates as commitments tends to push people to protect themselves: bigger numbers next time, or calling unfinished work done; either way the numbers tend to stop describing the work.
Scrum Guide 2020: a Product Backlog item that does not meet the Definition of Done is not presented at the Sprint Review and returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration.
claims.source_hint: Scrum Guide 2020, Commitment: Definition of Done

claims.text: Scrum Guide 2020: the Sprint Goal is the commitment for the Sprint Backlog; the Guide does not make individual estimates a commitment.
sprint-example.md line 31 says the team demonstrates on a test environment, not a personal machine; the retrospective does not mention the unfinished item.
Scrum Guide 2020: the Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint (the meeting at the end of the sprint where the team looks at how it worked).
